concept.summary: Insert a diffuse‑reflection NIR probe into the feed frame, collect spectra via a short‑length silica fiber to a bench‑top NIR spectrometer; optionally add a Raman probe at the same location for parallel data collection.
concept.probe: Diffuse‑reflection NIR probe (contact tip) and optional Raman fiber probe (785 nm excitation)
concept.location: Feed frame of the rotary tablet press, mounted on an existing process port
concept.fiberLink: Silica fiber (low‑OH) for NIR; silica or low‑loss fiber for Raman
concept.analyzer: Bench‑top NIR spectrometer (780–2500 nm) and Raman spectrometer (785 nm laser)

citations.quote: the probes are inserted directly into the process environment, such as the feed frame of a rotary tablet press.
As the powder blend passes the probe tip, the system captures spectra at high speeds without interrupting the production flow.
This setup allows the laboratory to track dynamic changes, such as the gradual increase in coating thickness or the homogenization of a multicomponent blend, in real-time.

spectralRange.summary: NIR absorption range 780–2500 nm (overtones of C‑H, N‑H, O‑H); Raman excitation 785 nm with Raman shift recorded in cm‑1.

citations.quote: NIR spectra (780–2500 nm) contain predominantly overtones and component bands of fundamental vibrations of molecules and atomic groups, such as -OH, -NH2=NH, -CH3, =CH2, ≥CH, etc., found in many organic and inorganic compounds.
The difference between the observed frequencies and the laser frequency is called the Raman shift, expressed in units of frequency–wavenumbers (cm-1).

steps: Collect representative powder samples covering the expected API concentration range.
Build a chemometric calibration model (e.g., PLS) and validate on held‑out samples.
Repeat the same with Raman (if probe is added) to assess complementary performance.
Evaluate model robustness to particle size and flow rate variations.
Acquire NIR diffuse‑reflection spectra in‑line using the proposed probe; simultaneously record reference API values with the existing lab assay.
feasibility.decisionBasis: If the NIR model meets the agreed‑upon prediction error on independent samples, it will be the preferred method; Raman results will inform whether a combined approach is needed. Agree two things separately with the customer before the test: the model accuracy required against the reference method, and the alarm or action threshold applied to the measured value.
